subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public configurable main-LLM retry/backoff policy, and should it live under provider request config, agent defaults, or remain as bounded built-in retry/fallback behavior?
rationale: This adds public config surface in provider routing, auth-profile, fallback, and availability behavior where repository policy requires a high bar and maintainer intent before cementing a contract.

options.title: Approve One Retry Contract
options.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, and focused tests before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep Built-In Only
options.body: Avoid a public retry knob for now and limit work to narrow built-in retry/fallback fixes with explicit idempotency boundaries.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Leave current manual retry/fallback behavior in place until maintainers decide the extra config surface is worth carrying.

recommendation.title: Approve One Retry Contract
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, and focused tests before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate for provider/config product direction based on current blame and related overload config history.
